item.title: Overview of Amos - God's Impartial Grace 🟢 NEW
item.description: Adapted from insights by Ray C. Stedman and other biblical reflections. Opening Story # On a warm afternoon, a community art studio hummed with quiet concentration. Children and adults sat at pottery wheels, each trying to coax beauty out of a stubborn lump of clay. Among them was a young girl who had saved her pocket money for weeks to make a gift “beautiful enough for Mum.” She pressed her palms against the clay, trying to shape it into a small vase. But the clay wobbled. She pressed harder. It bulged. She tried to steady it. It collapsed into a shapeless heap.

item.title: Overview of Joel - Hearing God in Seasons of Loss 🟢 NEW
item.description: Adapted from insights by Ray C. Stedman and other biblical reflections. Opening Story # She had never read the book of Joel. In fact, she had never even paused long enough to wonder what might be inside those three short chapters tucked quietly among the Minor Prophets. Her Bible reading habits had always gravitated toward the familiar, the comforting cadence of the Psalms, the narrative sweep of Genesis, the clarity of the Gospels. Joel, by contrast, felt like a sealed room in an old house: present, but unexplored; small, but somehow intimidating.

item.title: Overview of Hosea - Relentless Love 🟢 NEW
item.description: Adapted from insights by Ray C. Stedman and other biblical reflections. Opening Story - Entering Hosea Through a Human Heart # Leah had always imagined that marriage would be a safe harbor, a place where affection and stability formed the quiet architecture of daily life. Daniel, her husband, embodied that hope. He was gentle without being weak, steady without being dull, and devoted without being possessive. He loved her with a kind of patience that felt almost old‑world in a culture that rewarded speed, ambition, and self‑promotion.

item.title: Overview of Ezekiel - Wheels of Glory, Bones of Hope, Rivers of Life
item.description: Adapted from insights by Ray C. Stedman and other biblical reflections. Opening Story # A man once climbed onto his roof to adjust a stubborn television aerial. It was one of those quiet afternoons when the sky is calm, the neighbourhood still, and the mind occupied with small tasks that feel harmless. But as he leaned forward to tighten a bolt, his foot slipped on a patch of dust, and suddenly the world tilted beneath him. He slid toward the gutter, scrambling for anything to hold. His hands caught the eaves trough, and there he hung, suspended between the familiar safety of the roof and the unknown distance below.

item.title: Overview of Ecclesiastes – Finding Meaning Without God
item.description: Adapted from insights by Ray C. Stedman and other biblical reflections. Opening Story: When Life Feels Full but Hollow # Liam had never given much thought to the book of Ecclesiastes. It wasn’t that he disliked the Bible or held any particular resistance toward faith; rather, life had a way of filling his days with enough noise, movement, and responsibility that deeper questions were quietly pushed aside. He lived in Wollongong, close enough to the ocean that the sound of waves was a familiar backdrop, and from the outside, his life appeared steady and well‑arranged. He had a respectable job, a circle of friends who kept weekends lively, a gym routine that made him feel disciplined, and a growing savings account that reassured him he was doing what adults were supposed to do.

item.title: Overview of Job - Trusting God When You Have No Answers
item.description: Adapted from insights by Ray C. Stedman and other biblical reflections. Opening Story: When the Bottom Drops Out # Imagine a man named Daniel. He lives a steady, ordinary life in a small coastal town. He runs a family business, coaches his daughter’s netball team, and visits his parents every Sunday. Life isn’t perfect, but it’s stable, predictable, and safe.

item.title: Overview of 1 Chronicles - When God Becomes the Centre
item.description: Adapted from insights by Ray C. Stedman and other biblical reflections. Opening Story - Discovering the Family Chest # Sometimes the most important stories hide in places we don’t expect. Mira learned this the day she climbed into her grandfather’s dusty attic. She has come to clean it out after his passing. The room is dim, filled with boxes, old trunks, and the faint smell of cedar. She expects to find the usual things: faded clothes, broken tools, forgotten souvenirs.
